docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3864:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-2-opus.md:111:**Concrete user-visible case** (low-likelihood in v1 because sheet-delete API isn't exposed in workbook_runtime — see CC note below — but reachable through scenarios where a binder mis-resolution happens at the boundary, or through any future deletion path):
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3865:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-2-opus.md:127:**Reachability assessment.** Today, the workbook_runtime has no `delete_sheet` API (grep for `delete_sheet` / `remove_sheet` in workbook_runtime.rs returns 0 production paths). So the deleted-sheet case isn't exercisable from end-user formulas. BUT: any future deletion API will need to either (a) bring this in scope as a regression OR (b) ship with this materializer arm pre-fixed. Also: the WorkbookEnv's `read_cell` returns `Blank` for missing cells in an existing sheet — that's correct and not an error. The error-path is reachable only via the missing-sheet branch today.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3868:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-2-opus.md:498:**Recommendation:** Update design § 5.6 to use `av.rows() as f64` and `av.cols() as f64` to match the actual API. Or, alternatively, add `pub fn shape(&self) -> (u32, u32) { (self.rows, self.cols) }` to ArrayValue and update the impl. The former is lower-impact.
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3886:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:94:Any code that attempts to print a post-bind AST (where `SheetRef::Name` has been resolved to `SheetRef::Id` by the binder) will panic. The rename rewrite round-trip in `workbook_runtime.rs:85–108` correctly uses a pre-bind parse (never binds before printing), so the panic is not triggered in the current happy path. However, this is a latent footgun for any future caller that binds then prints. The design acknowledges this with a "future `print_with_resolver` API" note, but no tracking issue exists. Severity: MEDIUM (no current crash path, but the API is a trap for future contributors).
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3889:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:297:- The design's `print_with_resolver` API is not implemented (future work, acknowledged).
docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3890:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:322:The rename rewrite round-trip does not trigger this because it never binds before printing. However, the footgun is real: any future code that binds a formula (converting `Name` → `Id`) then attempts to print the AST will panic. Options: (a) implement `print_with_resolver` API that takes a `SheetId → &str` resolver, or (b) add a `#[doc(hidden)]` warning and a prominent comment on `print_sheet_prefix` noting the `Id` panic, and file a tracking issue. For W5-93 close, (b) is acceptable.

docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:339:./docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:23:The current qbook format uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and its documented policy says any future additive field requires a schema bump. Adding `scope` to `NamedEntry` or `NamedTargetWire` while keeping schema v4 means older v4 readers will treat the new file as "supported schema 4" and then fail during TOML deserialization with an unknown field, not with `UnsupportedSchema`. That is exactly the forward-compat hygiene the current schema policy was designed to avoid.

Per-sheet generation is design § 10.5 / Codex MEDIUM-7 future polish; full flush is acceptable at edit rate.

docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:454:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).

docs/audits/2026-05-13-finalization-merged-plan.md:58:The W5-50 → W5-52 arc is the case study. W5-50 shipped under "GAP-G-01 closed" framing. The `on_clear_formula` clear-path bug shipped silently. W5-52 mega-audit (Codex + Sonnet) caught it because both auditors independently flagged the same staleness class on the clear path. Without the parallel pattern, a future regression in this surface would have been the first time the bug surfaced — much later, in user code.

docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:148:This means: if a future refactor reverts the `"SUBTOTAL"` entry in `is_aggregate_function`, the workspace would still pass `cargo test --workspace`. The invariant test (`is_aggregate_function_lists_only_registered_aggregates`) only checks `lookup_range_aware("SUBTOTAL").is_some()` — that's just a registry-lookup smoke test, not a binder-path test. The HIGH-001 closure has zero test armor.
docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:154:The outer SUBTOTAL sums 3 (inner SUBTOTAL result) + 3 = 6. Excel canon: outer would skip nested-SUBTOTAL → return just 3. **This is the documented v1 divergence** (`range_fns.rs:1953-1972` block comment). Fine — documented. But there's also NO test pinning this divergence. A future refactor that accidentally implements nested-skip would break workbook compat with no test failure.
docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:179:**Severity rationale:** HIGH. A closure that doesn't test the path it claims to fix is a partial fix. The matrix and master-plan both believe SUBTOTAL is fully shipped. The fix is mechanical (one positive test). The risk is that a future refactor regresses the admission without anyone noticing.
docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:251:**Detail:** Compiled probe: `BINOM.INV(10, 1, 0.5)` → `Error(Num)`. The `(0.0..1.0)` half-open range explicitly excludes p=1.0. But at p=1.0 the binomial is degenerate at `n` (every trial succeeds) so `inverse_cdf(alpha)` for any alpha ∈ (0,1) is exactly `n`. The W5-D-4.1 closure for p=0 (line 1169) added a short-circuit `if p == 0.0 || n == 0 { return Value::number(0.0); }`. The corresponding p=1 short-circuit was NOT added.
docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:253:Codex W5-D-4 audit (HIGH-1 closure for p=0) only mentioned p=0; the p=1 case was a missed corner. Microsoft's BINOM.INV doc says `Probability_s >= 0` AND `Probability_s <= 1` (inclusive both ends). The engine's strict-upper diverges from Microsoft.
docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:288:**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. The bulk of the corners are correct; the consolidating doc would prevent future maintainers from re-debugging these. Not a code bug, but a structural debt.
docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:304:The divergence is documented but not pinned by a test. A future refactor that walks `ExprPlan` to detect nested-SUBTOTAL calls (a legitimate path forward toward Excel parity) would silently change behavior. The test would catch the engine→Excel transition.
docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:398:**Detail:** Per CLAUDE.md memory rules, this is acceptable (memory is a snapshot, not a session log). But future sessions reading the memory pointer will get an outdated baseline. The `quantbook_engine_phase4_10_v1_260_shipped.md` file is the authoritative pointer for the current state.
docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:420:1. **Math kernel correctness**: All 38 Wave 3 distribution fns and the 22 closeout-batch fns produce correct results on textbook anchors and degrade gracefully on degenerate inputs. The W5-D-1.1, W5-D-4.1, W5-D-5.1, W5-D-7.1, W5-D-8.1, W5-D-11.1, W5-D-12.1 closures all correctly addressed their per-batch audit findings at the code level.
docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-49-50-51-megaudit-sonnet.md:108:The implementation correctly uses `args[0]` as `x` and `args[1]` as `y` (Excel order: `ATAN2(x_num, y_num)`), and the actual call is `y.atan2(x)`. The doc title inverts the argument labels, which is confusing to anyone reading the signature. The function body, the inline comment at line 843, and the test `atan2_basic_quadrants` are all correct. This is a documentation-only error but could mislead a future maintainer.
docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-49-50-51-megaudit-sonnet.md:152:However, as noted in the brief: Phase 3.3 sets `range.sheet = Some(_)` always during binding, so the `unwrap_or(fs)` fallback is currently unreachable. The future cross-sheet case (Phase 4.6) will work correctly if the binder sets `sheet: Some(target_sheet)` for cross-sheet refs. The one risk: if a future binder sets `sheet: None` for cross-sheet refs and relies on context, the supplemental builder would incorrectly scope G's to F's sheet. This is a latent risk, not a current bug.
docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-49-50-51-megaudit-sonnet.md:193:5. **`remove_formula_deps` docstring**: clarify that the contract "revoked separately by the caller" applies to `extract_and_register_deps` only, and that `on_clear_formula` must also honor it. (This is now fixed by item #1, but the docstring should be updated to avoid future confusion.)
docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-self.md:166:**Detail:** A test named "preserves" that asserts only sheet count is a documentation lie. A future refactor that drops all cell values on export would PASS this test. Per the W5-D-13.1 audit-discipline Rule 3 ("lex+parse+bind+eval coverage"), round-trip tests must assert SEMANTIC equivalence end-to-end.

     1	//! `Presence` — per-peer ephemeral cursor + selection state.
     2	//!
     3	//! **Phase 5.6 V1 (2026-05-19, ship):** implements the
     4	//! audit-closed design at `docs/architecture/crdt-data-model.md`
     5	//! § Presence container.
     6	//!
     7	//! Each peer's state lives in the `"presence"` LoroMap inside the
     8	//! shared `LoroDoc`. Keys are the peer-id 16-hex `Display` form
     9	//! (e.g. `"0000000000000001"`); values are JSON-serialized
    10	//! [`PresenceState`] blobs. Loro's LoroMap merge is LWW per key,
    11	//! which gives the desired "last position update wins per peer"
    12	//! semantics.
    13	//!
    14	//! ## Persistence
    15	//!
    16	//! Presence updates DO survive `OpLog::export_bytes` /
    17	//! `import_bytes` (they live in the same `LoroDoc`), but the
    18	//! `.qbook` envelope (`ql_io::oplog_persistence`) writes the
    19	//! whole snapshot, so cold-restart presence will land in the new
    20	//! session. Phase 5.6 V2 may add envelope-level filtering if
    21	//! "rejoin and see stale presence" turns out to be undesirable
    22	//! UX; V1 keeps the data so the multi-peer round-trip test
    23	//! pattern works.
    24	//!
    25	//! ## Concurrency
    26	//!
    27	//! Two peers updating their OWN keys never conflict — LoroMap is
    28	//! per-key LWW and the keys are distinct by construction. Two
    29	//! peers updating the SAME key (i.e. one peer impersonating
    30	//! another by sharing the same `PeerId`) is undefined behavior
    31	//! per the Loro duplicate-peer-id pitfall already documented at
    32	//! `OpLog::set_peer_id` and `CollabSession::new`.
    33	//!
    34	//! ## Forward work (NOT in V1)
    35	//!
    36	//! - Phase 5.6 V2: presence-changed callback (Loro `subscribe`
    37	//!   on the `"presence"` container). V1 callers poll via
    38	//!   [`crate::CollabSession::peer_presence`].
    39	//! - Phase 5.7: IDE wires per-peer color + name from a separate
    40	//!   metadata layer (presence map only holds position state).
    41	
    42	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    43	use thiserror::Error;
    44	
    45	use crate::peer::PeerId;
    46	
    47	/// Per-peer ephemeral state: cursor position + active selection +
    48	/// typing indicator.
    49	///
    50	/// Coordinates are sheet-local (NOT global). `(sheet, row, col)`
    51	/// is the cursor; `(selection_end_row, selection_end_col)`
    52	/// together with the cursor defines a rectangular selection. When
    53	/// no range is selected, set `selection_end_row = row` and
    54	/// `selection_end_col = col` (the selection collapses to the
    55	/// cursor cell).
    56	///
    57	/// `typing` is a soft hint for the IDE — true while the user is
    58	/// mid-edit (formula bar focused or in-cell edit mode), false
    59	/// otherwise. Consumers may use it to render a different cursor
    60	/// style without relying on op-log signals.
    61	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    62	pub struct PresenceState {
    63	    /// 0-indexed sheet id.
    64	    pub sheet: u16,
    65	    /// 0-indexed row of the cursor cell.
    66	    pub row: u32,
    67	    /// 0-indexed column of the cursor cell.
    68	    pub col: u32,
    69	    /// 0-indexed row of the selection rectangle's opposite corner.
    70	    /// Equals `row` when the selection collapses to a single cell.
    71	    pub selection_end_row: u32,
    72	    /// 0-indexed column of the selection rectangle's opposite corner.
    73	    /// Equals `col` when the selection collapses to a single cell.
    74	    pub selection_end_col: u32,
    75	    /// True while the peer is actively editing (formula bar focused
    76	    /// or in-cell edit mode).
    77	    pub typing: bool,
    78	}
    79	
    80	impl PresenceState {
    81	    /// Construct a `PresenceState` with a single-cell selection
    82	    /// (selection_end_* = row/col) and `typing = false`.
    83	    ///
    84	    /// Convenient for "cursor moved to A1" updates that don't
    85	    /// require building a full struct.
    86	    pub const fn at_cell(sheet: u16, row: u32, col: u32) -> Self {
    87	        Self {
    88	            sheet,
    89	            row,
    90	            col,
    91	            selection_end_row: row,
    92	            selection_end_col: col,
    93	            typing: false,
    94	        }
    95	    }
    96	
    97	    /// True if the selection collapses to a single cell.
    98	    pub fn is_single_cell(&self) -> bool {
    99	        self.selection_end_row == self.row && self.selection_end_col == self.col
   100	    }
   101	}
   102	
   103	/// Errors emitted by `Presence` operations.
   104	#[derive(Debug, Error)]
   105	#[non_exhaustive]
   106	pub enum PresenceError {
   107	    /// JSON serialization of `PresenceState` failed. Should be
   108	    /// unreachable for well-formed `PresenceState` (all fields
   109	    /// are primitives).
   110	    #[error("presence serialize error: {0}")]
   111	    Serialize(#[source] serde_json::Error),
   112	
   113	    /// JSON deserialization of a presence blob failed. Indicates a
   114	    /// peer wrote an incompatible shape (version drift between
   115	    /// peers, OR corrupted snapshot).
   116	    #[error("presence deserialize error for peer {peer_key}: {source}")]
   117	    Deserialize {
   118	        peer_key: String,
   119	        #[source]
   120	        source: serde_json::Error,
   121	    },
   122	
   123	    /// Wrapped `OpLogError` — the underlying Loro container
   124	    /// access (insert / get / delete) failed.
   125	    #[error("presence op log error: {0}")]
   126	    OpLog(#[from] ql_oplog::OpLogError),
   127	
   128	    /// A peer key in the `"presence"` LoroMap could not be parsed
   129	    /// back into a `PeerId`. Indicates that another producer wrote
   130	    /// a non-16-hex-u64 key into the map — incompatible with this
   131	    /// version's encoding.
   132	    #[error("presence peer-key parse error: {peer_key:?} ({source})")]
   133	    PeerKeyParse {
   134	        peer_key: String,
   135	        #[source]
   136	        source: std::num::ParseIntError,
   137	    },
   138	}
   139	
   140	/// Format a `PeerId` as its presence-map key.
   141	///
   142	/// Uses the 16-hex `Display` form (e.g. `"0000000000000001"`).
   143	/// Matches the format used elsewhere in the engine (logs,
   144	/// debug output) so a presence dump is greppable.
   145	pub(crate) fn peer_key(peer: PeerId) -> String {
   146	    format!("{peer}")
   147	}
   148	
   149	/// Parse a presence-map key back into a `PeerId`.
   150	///
   151	/// Inverse of [`peer_key`]. Returns [`PresenceError::PeerKeyParse`]
   152	/// if the key isn't 16-hex-digit u64.
   153	pub(crate) fn parse_peer_key(key: &str) -> Result<PeerId, PresenceError> {
   154	    let raw = u64::from_str_radix(key, 16).map_err(|source| PresenceError::PeerKeyParse {
   155	        peer_key: key.to_owned(),
   156	        source,
   157	    })?;
   158	    Ok(PeerId::new(raw))
   159	}
   160	
   161	#[cfg(test)]
   162	mod tests {
   163	    use super::*;
   164	
   165	    #[test]
   166	    fn at_cell_collapses_selection() {
   167	        let s = PresenceState::at_cell(0, 3, 4);
   168	        assert_eq!(s.sheet, 0);
   169	        assert_eq!(s.row, 3);
   170	        assert_eq!(s.col, 4);
   171	        assert!(s.is_single_cell());
   172	        assert!(!s.typing);
   173	    }
   174	
   175	    #[test]
   176	    fn range_selection_detected() {
   177	        let s = PresenceState {
   178	            sheet: 0,
   179	            row: 0,
   180	            col: 0,
   181	            selection_end_row: 5,
   182	            selection_end_col: 5,
   183	            typing: false,
   184	        };
   185	        assert!(!s.is_single_cell());
   186	    }
   187	
   188	    #[test]
   189	    fn serde_round_trip() {
   190	        let s = PresenceState {
   191	            sheet: 2,
   192	            row: 100,
   193	            col: 26,
   194	            selection_end_row: 200,
   195	            selection_end_col: 27,
   196	            typing: true,
   197	        };
   198	        let json = serde_json::to_string(&s).unwrap();
   199	        let parsed: PresenceState = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
   200	        assert_eq!(s, parsed);
   201	    }
   202	
   203	    #[test]
   204	    fn peer_key_round_trip() {
   205	        let p = PeerId::new(0x1234_5678_9abc_def0);
   206	        let key = peer_key(p);
   207	        assert_eq!(key, "123456789abcdef0");
   208	        let parsed = parse_peer_key(&key).unwrap();
   209	        assert_eq!(parsed, p);
   210	    }
   211	
   212	    #[test]
   213	    fn peer_key_parse_rejects_garbage() {
   214	        let result = parse_peer_key("not-a-peer-id");
   215	        assert!(matches!(result, Err(PresenceError::PeerKeyParse { .. })));
   216	    }
   217	}

     1	//! `OpLog` — Loro-backed append-only operation log.
     2	//!
     3	//! Phase 2A.3.a (2026-05-12): scaffolding-only API. The log stores ops as
     4	//! JSON-encoded strings inside a single Loro `LoroList` container named
     5	//! `"ops"`. Each `OpLog::append` call serializes the `Op`, pushes a string
     6	//! into the list, and commits the Loro doc.
     7	//!
     8	//! ## Why JSON-in-Loro
     9	//!
    10	//! Per Round 7 architectural lock T1-D05, Loro is reserved for the op log
    11	//! layer. Phase 2A.3.a aims for minimum viable scaffolding — full CRDT
    12	//! semantics (LoroMap-per-op with typed fields) is reserved for Phase 5+
    13	//! when inter-peer merging becomes load-bearing. The JSON layer is
    14	//! invisible to callers: they see typed `Op` values via `iter`.
    15	//!
    16	//! ## Persistence
    17	//!
    18	//! `export_bytes` produces a `Vec<u8>` via `ExportMode::Snapshot`. The
    19	//! resulting blob includes the full state plus history; suitable for
    20	//! `oplog.bin` on-disk persistence (Phase 2A.3.c).
    21	//!
    22	//! `import_bytes` reconstructs an `OpLog` from such a blob. The reader
    23	//! probes the `"ops"` LoroList; if absent (or the wrong shape), the
    24	//! import returns `OpLogError::SchemaMismatch`.
    25	
    26	use loro::{ExportMode, LoroDoc, LoroList, LoroValue, ValueOrContainer};
    27	
    28	use crate::error::OpLogError;
    29	use crate::op::Op;
    30	
    31	/// The Loro container name our ops live under. Hard-coded; Phase 5+
    32	/// CRDT-level refactoring may add more containers (versions, peer state,
    33	/// etc.) but `"ops"` is reserved.
    34	const OPS_CONTAINER: &str = "ops";
    35	
    36	/// **Phase 5.6 (2026-05-19):** Loro container name for the per-peer
    37	/// ephemeral presence map (cursor + selection + typing indicator).
    38	/// Per the audit-closed Phase 5.1 design at
    39	/// `docs/architecture/crdt-data-model.md` § Presence container.
    40	/// Keys are peer-id strings; values are opaque JSON blobs (the
    41	/// typed `PresenceState` encoding lives in `ql_collab::presence`).
    42	const PRESENCE_CONTAINER: &str = "presence";
    43	
    44	/// Append-only operation log backed by Loro.
    45	///
    46	/// Construct via `OpLog::new()` for a fresh log or `OpLog::import_bytes(...)`
    47	/// to reconstruct from a persisted snapshot. Mutations go through `append`;
    48	/// reads through `iter` / `len` / `is_empty`.
    49	pub struct OpLog {
    50	    doc: LoroDoc,
    51	    /// Cached count to avoid round-tripping into Loro for `len()`. Always
    52	    /// equal to `doc.get_list(OPS_CONTAINER).len()`; updated on append
    53	    /// and on import.
    54	    cached_len: usize,
    55	}
    56	
    57	impl std::fmt::Debug for OpLog {
    58	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
    59	        f.debug_struct("OpLog")
    60	            .field("cached_len", &self.cached_len)
    61	            .field("doc", &"<LoroDoc>")
    62	            .finish()
    63	    }
    64	}
    65	
    66	impl Default for OpLog {
    67	    fn default() -> Self {
    68	        Self::new()
    69	    }
    70	}
    71	
    72	impl OpLog {
    73	    /// Construct an empty log.
    74	    pub fn new() -> Self {
    75	        Self {
    76	            doc: LoroDoc::new(),
    77	            cached_len: 0,
    78	        }
    79	    }
    80	
    81	    /// Append one `Op` to the log. Serializes via `serde_json`, stores as
    82	    /// a `LoroValue::String` in the `"ops"` LoroList, and commits the
    83	    /// underlying Loro doc.
    84	    pub fn append(&mut self, op: Op) -> Result<(), OpLogError> {
    85	        let json = serde_json::to_string(&op).map_err(OpLogError::Serialize)?;
    86	        let list: LoroList = self.doc.get_list(OPS_CONTAINER);
    87	        list.push(LoroValue::from(json.as_str()))?;
    88	        self.doc.commit();
    89	        self.cached_len += 1;
    90	        Ok(())
    91	    }
    92	
    93	    /// Iterate the log in append order. Each yielded item is a
    94	    /// `Result<Op, OpLogError>` — a deserialization failure yields
    95	    /// `Err(OpLogError::Deserialize { index, source })` and iteration
    96	    /// continues (no short-circuit). Callers wanting fail-fast can use
    97	    /// `iter().collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()`.
    98	    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Result<Op, OpLogError>> + '_ {
    99	        let list: LoroList = self.doc.get_list(OPS_CONTAINER);
   100	        let len = list.len();
   101	        (0..len).map(move |index| {
   102	            let entry = list.get(index).ok_or(OpLogError::SchemaMismatch(
   103	                "ops LoroList lost an entry between len() and get()",
   104	            ))?;
   105	            let value = match entry {
   106	                ValueOrContainer::Value(v) => v,
   107	                ValueOrContainer::Container(_) => {
   108	                    return Err(OpLogError::SchemaMismatch(
   109	                        "ops LoroList holds a container; expected JSON-string values",
   110	                    ));
   111	                }
   112	            };
   113	            let s = match value {
   114	                LoroValue::String(s) => s,
   115	                _ => {
   116	                    return Err(OpLogError::SchemaMismatch(
   117	                        "ops LoroList holds a non-string LoroValue; expected JSON-string",
   118	                    ));
   119	                }
   120	            };

   200	    /// container; current API only writes strings).
   201	    pub fn presence_get(&self, peer_key: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, OpLogError> {

   203	        let Some(entry) = map.get(peer_key) else {

   207	            ValueOrContainer::Value(v) => v,
   208	            ValueOrContainer::Container(_) => {

   210	                    "presence LoroMap holds a container value; expected JSON string",
   211	                ));
   212	            }
   213	        };

   215	            LoroValue::String(s) => Ok(Some(s.to_string())),

    28	/// allocation unless your server enforces uniqueness explicitly.

     2	//!

    12	//!   poll [`crate::Transport::try_recv`] for remote bytes →
    13	//!   `merge_bytes`.
    14	//! - **Phase 5.6** — presence map updates (per-peer cursor + selection).
    15	//! - **Phase 5.7** — IDE binding: `CollabSession` becomes the engine
    16	//!   handle that the IDE attaches to each open workbook.
    17	//!
    18	//! What ships in 5.2.a (5.2.b update 2026-05-19):

    28	//!   ops in the imported snapshot retain their original

    30	//! - `append_op(&mut self, Op)` — local append; delegates to

   116	    ///   concurrent session — see `OpLog::set_peer_id` for details.
   117	    /// - `PeerId(u64::MAX)` is reserved.
   118	    pub fn from_snapshot(peer_id: PeerId, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, CollabSessionError> {
   119	        let log = OpLog::import_bytes(bytes)?;
   120	        log.set_peer_id(peer_id.as_u64())?;
   121	        Ok(Self { peer_id, log })
   122	    }
   123	
   124	    /// Stable peer id assigned at session creation.
   125	    pub fn peer_id(&self) -> PeerId {
   126	        self.peer_id
   127	    }
   128	
   129	    /// Append a local op. Delegates to `OpLog::append`. Phase 5.5
   130	    /// will additionally push the appended bytes through the
   131	    /// attached `Transport`; 5.2.a leaves transport integration to
   132	    /// the caller.
   133	    pub fn append_op(&mut self, op: Op) -> Result<(), CollabSessionError> {
   134	        self.log.append(op)?;
   135	        Ok(())
   136	    }
   137	
   138	    /// Merge a remote peer's snapshot into this session's log. Loro's
   139	    /// CRDT preserves both peers' concurrent appends in deterministic
   140	    /// causal order (Fugue/origin-based with peer-id tiebreaker per
   141	    /// Phase 5.1 audit Codex V1). Returns the new `len()` after merge.
   142	    pub fn merge_bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, CollabSessionError> {
   143	        Ok(self.log.merge_bytes(bytes)?)
   144	    }
   145	
   146	    /// Produce a Loro snapshot blob suitable for transport to other
   147	    /// peers OR for `.qbook/oplog.bin` persistence.
   148	    pub fn export_bytes(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CollabSessionError> {
   149	        Ok(self.log.export_bytes()?)
   150	    }
   151	
   152	    /// Borrow the underlying `OpLog` for replay against a `Workbook`.
   153	    ///
   154	    /// Typical usage:
   155	    /// ```ignore
   156	    /// let session = CollabSession::from_snapshot(peer_id, &bytes)?;
   157	    /// let mut wb = ql_storage::Workbook::new();
   158	    /// let reg = ql_functions::default_registry();
   159	    /// ql_oplog::replay_into(session.op_log(), &mut wb, &reg)?;
   160	    /// ```
   161	    pub fn op_log(&self) -> &OpLog {
   162	        &self.log
   163	    }
   164	
   165	    /// Current number of ops in the log. Cheap (cached).
   166	    pub fn op_count(&self) -> usize {
   167	        self.log.len()
   168	    }
   169	
   170	    /// True iff the log has no ops (session just opened, no edits yet).
   171	    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
   172	        self.log.is_empty()
   173	    }
   174	
   175	    /// **Phase 5.6 V1 (2026-05-19):** write this session's own
   176	    /// presence state into the shared `"presence"` LoroMap.
   177	    ///
   178	    /// Uses the session's `PeerId` as the map key (16-hex
   179	    /// `Display` form). Subsequent calls overwrite the previous
   180	    /// value (LWW per peer); merges with other peers'
   181	    /// presence writes preserve all distinct peers.
   182	    pub fn update_presence(&mut self, state: PresenceState) -> Result<(), CollabSessionError> {
   183	        let key = presence::peer_key(self.peer_id);
   184	        let json = serde_json::to_string(&state).map_err(PresenceError::Serialize)?;
   185	        self.log.presence_set(&key, &json)?;
   186	        Ok(())
   187	    }
   188	
   189	    /// **Phase 5.6 V1 (2026-05-19):** read a peer's most recent
   190	    /// presence state. Returns `Ok(None)` if the peer has never
   191	    /// updated its presence in this session (or has been removed
   192	    /// via `clear_presence`).
   193	    pub fn peer_presence(&self, peer: PeerId) -> Result<Option<PresenceState>, CollabSessionError> {
   194	        let key = presence::peer_key(peer);
   195	        let Some(json) = self.log.presence_get(&key)? else {
   196	            return Ok(None);
   197	        };
   198	        let state: PresenceState =
   199	            serde_json::from_str(&json).map_err(|source| PresenceError::Deserialize {
   200	                peer_key: key,
   201	                source,
   202	            })?;
   203	        Ok(Some(state))
   204	    }
   205	
   206	    /// **Phase 5.6 V1 (2026-05-19):** remove this session's own
   207	    /// presence entry from the shared map. Use this when the
   208	    /// peer leaves the session (window close, disconnect). After
   209	    /// removal, other peers' `peer_presence(self_id)` returns
   210	    /// `Ok(None)`.
   211	    pub fn clear_presence(&mut self) -> Result<(), CollabSessionError> {
   212	        let key = presence::peer_key(self.peer_id);
   213	        self.log.presence_remove(&key)?;
   214	        Ok(())
   215	    }
   216	
   217	    /// **Phase 5.6 V1 (2026-05-19):** list every peer with a
   218	    /// presence entry in the shared map.
   219	    ///
   220	    /// Order is Loro's iteration order. Sort the result if you
   221	    /// need determinism.
   222	    ///
   223	    /// Returns `Err(CollabSessionError::Presence(PresenceError::PeerKeyParse))`
   224	    /// if a key in the map can't be parsed as a `PeerId` (only
   225	    /// reachable if a future writer uses an incompatible
   226	    /// encoding).
   227	    pub fn peers_with_presence(&self) -> Result<Vec<PeerId>, CollabSessionError> {
   228	        let keys = self.log.presence_peers();
   229	        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(keys.len());
   230	        for k in keys {
   231	            out.push(presence::parse_peer_key(&k)?);
   232	        }
   233	        Ok(out)
   234	    }
   235	}

   241	            .field("op_count", &self.log.len())
   242	            .finish()
   243	    }

 succeeded in 278ms:

   215	
   216	### Presence container: `"presence"` LoroMap (per-peer ephemeral)
   217	
   218	New for Phase 5.6. Holds the per-peer cursor + selection +
   219	typing indicator. Keys are peer-IDs (UUIDs); values are JSON
   220	blobs with `{sheet, row, col, selection_end_row,
   221	selection_end_col, typing: bool}`.
   222	
   223	```
   224	LoroDoc
   225	├── LoroList "ops"
   226	└── LoroMap "presence"
   227	    ├── "peer-uuid-A": "{\"sheet\":0,\"row\":3,\"col\":2,...}"
   228	    └── "peer-uuid-B": "{\"sheet\":1,\"row\":0,\"col\":0,...}"
   229	```
   230	
   231	**Why MOM (Map of Maps) is wrong for cells but right for presence**:
   232	- Cells need ordering-aware merge (Tier C1 cycle detection
   233	  depends on op-log order; spill-anchor invariants depend on
   234	  set_formula-before-set_value-at-target ordering). Op-log
   235	  preserves this.
   236	- Presence is ephemeral and unordered — each peer overwrites
   237	  its own key. LoroMap LWW merge gives "last position update
   238	  wins per peer," which is exactly the desired semantic.
   239	
   240	Presence updates do NOT persist across `.qbook` save/load.
   241	Phase 5.6 wires the in-memory presence map; `.qbook` envelope
   242	v8 may or may not persist it depending on whether the use case
   243	demands "rejoin a session and see where teammates were" — out
   244	of 5.1 scope.
   245	
   246	### Snapshot container: `"snapshot"` LoroMap (reserved, V2)
   247	
   248	Phase 5 V2 may introduce a snapshot container that holds a
   249	compact representation of the workbook state at a recent
   250	version vector. Replay against a snapshot skips ops older than
    95	  load path. Affects Phase 5 because replay uses
    96	  `recompute_all` per `ql-oplog::replay::replay_into`.
    97	  **Recommendation: close C1 before 5.2.**
    98	- **C2.** BatchCommit depth guard. Pair with C1.

   139	        self.child_containers.contains_key(id)
   140	    }
   141	
   142	    fn get_child_containers(&self) -> Vec<ContainerID> {
   143	        let mut ans = Vec::new();
   144	        for (_, value) in self.map.iter() {
   145	            if let Some(LoroValue::Container(x)) = &value.value {
   146	                ans.push(x.clone());
   147	            }
   148	        }
   149	        ans
   150	    }

   156	
   157	impl MapState {
   158	    pub fn new(idx: ContainerIdx) -> Self {
   159	        Self {
   160	            idx,
   161	            map: Default::default(),
   162	            child_containers: Default::default(),
   163	            size: 0,
   164	        }
   165	    }
   166	
   167	    pub fn insert(&mut self, key: InternalString, value: MapValue) -> Option<MapValue> {
   168	        let value_yes = value.value.is_some();
   169	        if let Some(LoroValue::Container(id)) = &value.value {
   170	            self.child_containers.insert(id.clone(), key.clone());
   171	        }
   172	
   173	        let result = self.map.insert(key.clone(), value);
   174	        if let Some(Some(LoroValue::Container(c))) = result.as_ref().map(|x| &x.value) {
   175	            self.child_containers.remove(c);
   176	        }
   177	
   178	        match (&result, value_yes) {
   179	            (Some(x), true) => {
   180	                if x.value.is_none() {
   181	                    self.size += 1;
   182	                }
   183	            }
   184	            (None, true) => {
   185	                self.size += 1;
   186	            }
   187	            (Some(x), false) => {
   188	                if x.value.is_some() {
   189	                    self.size -= 1;
   190	                }
   191	            }
   192	            _ => {}
   193	        };
   194	
   195	        result
   196	    }
   197	
   198	    pub fn remove(&mut self, key: &InternalString) {
   199	        let result = self.map.remove(key);
   200	        if let Some(x) = result {
   201	            if x.value.is_some() {
   202	                self.size -= 1;
   203	            }
   204	            if let Some(LoroValue::Container(id)) = x.value {
   205	                self.child_containers.remove(&id);
   206	            }
   207	        };
   208	    }
   209	
   210	    pub fn iter(&self) -> std::collections::btree_map::Iter<'_, InternalString, MapValue> {
   211	        self.map.iter()
   212	    }
   213	
   214	    fn to_map(&self) -> FxHashMap<String, LoroValue> {
   215	        let mut ans = FxHashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(self.len(), Default::default());
   216	        for (key, value) in self.map.iter() {
   217	            if value.value.is_none() {
   218	                continue;
   219	            }
   220	
   221	            ans.insert(key.to_string(), value.value.as_ref().cloned().unwrap());
   222	        }
   223	
   224	        ans
   225	    }
   226	
   227	    pub fn get(&self, k: &str) -> Option<&LoroValue> {
   228	        match self.map.get(&k.into()) {
   229	            Some(value) => match &value.value {
   230	                Some(v) => Some(v),
   231	                None => None,
   232	            },
   233	            None => None,
   234	        }
   235	    }
   236	
   237	    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
   238	        self.size
   239	    }

   247	
   248	    use loro_common::{InternalString, LoroValue};
   249	    use rustc_hash::{FxHashMap, FxHashSet};
   250	    use serde_columnar::Itertools;

   259	
   260	    impl FastStateSnapshot for MapState {
   261	        fn encode_snapshot_fast<W: std::io::prelude::Write>(&mut self, mut w: W) {
   262	            // 1. LoroValue
   263	            // 2. Vec<String> keys_with_none_value
   264	            // 3. leb128 peer_num + peers (in u64)
   265	            // 3. Groups of (leb128 peer_idx, leb128 lamport), each has a respective map entry
   266	            //    from either 1 or 2 when they all sorted by the key strings
   267	            let value = self.get_value().into_map().unwrap();
   268	            postcard::to_io(&*value, &mut w).unwrap();
   269	
   270	            let keys_with_none_value = self
   271	                .map
   272	                .iter()
   273	                .filter_map(|(k, v)| if v.value.is_some() { None } else { Some(k) })
   274	                .collect_vec();
   275	            postcard::to_io(&keys_with_none_value, &mut w).unwrap();
   276	            let mut peer_register = ValueRegister::new();
   277	            for v in self.map.values() {
   278	                peer_register.register(&v.peer);
   279	            }
   280	
   281	            leb128::write::unsigned(&mut w, peer_register.vec().len() as u64).unwrap();
   282	            for p in peer_register.vec() {
   283	                w.write_all(&p.to_le_bytes()).unwrap();
   284	            }
   285	            let mut keys: Vec<&InternalString> = self.map.keys().collect();
   286	            keys.sort_unstable();
   287	            for key in keys.into_iter() {
   288	                let value = self.map.get(key).unwrap();
   289	                let peer_idx = peer_register.register(&value.peer);
   290	                leb128::write::unsigned(&mut w, peer_idx as u64).unwrap();
   291	                leb128::write::unsigned(&mut w, value.lamp as u64).unwrap();
   292	            }
   293	        }
   294	
   295	        fn decode_value(bytes: &[u8]) -> loro_common::LoroResult<(loro_common::LoroValue, &[u8])> {
   296	            let (value, bytes) = postcard::take_from_bytes::<FxHashMap<String, LoroValue>>(bytes)
   297	                .map_err(|_| {
   298	                loro_common::LoroError::DecodeError(
   299	                    "Decode map value failed".to_string().into_boxed_str(),
   300	                )
   301	            })?;
   302	            Ok((LoroValue::Map(value.into()), bytes))
   303	        }
   304	
   305	        fn decode_snapshot_fast(
   306	            idx: crate::container::idx::ContainerIdx,
   307	            (value, bytes): (loro_common::LoroValue, &[u8]),
   308	            _ctx: ContainerCreationContext,
   309	        ) -> loro_common::LoroResult<Self>
   310	        where
   311	            Self: Sized,
   312	        {
   313	            let value = value.into_map().unwrap();
   314	            // keys_with_none_value
   315	            let (keys_with_none_value, mut bytes) =
   316	                postcard::take_from_bytes::<Vec<InternalString>>(bytes).map_err(|_| {
   317	                    loro_common::LoroError::DecodeError(
   318	                        "Decode map keys_with_none_value failed"
   319	                            .to_string()
   320	                            .into_boxed_str(),
   321	                    )
   322	                })?;
   323	            let keys_with_none_value: FxHashSet<_> = keys_with_none_value.into_iter().collect();
   324	
   325	            // peers
   326	            let peer_count = leb128::read::unsigned(&mut bytes).unwrap() as usize;
   327	            let mut peers = Vec::with_capacity(peer_count);
   328	            for _ in 0..peer_count {
   329	                let peer = u64::from_le_bytes(bytes[..8].try_into().unwrap());
   330	                bytes = &bytes[8..];
   331	                peers.push(peer);
   332	            }
   333	
   334	            //
   335	            let mut ans = MapState::new(idx);
   336	            let mut keys: Vec<_> = value.keys().map(|x| x.as_str().into()).collect();
   337	            keys.extend(keys_with_none_value.iter().cloned());
   338	            keys.sort_unstable();
   339	
   340	            for key in keys {
   341	                let peer_idx = leb128::read::unsigned(&mut bytes).unwrap() as usize;
   342	                let lamp = leb128::read::unsigned(&mut bytes).unwrap() as u32;
   343	                let peer = peers[peer_idx];
   344	
   345	                if keys_with_none_value.contains(&key) {
   346	                    ans.insert(
   347	                        key,
   348	                        MapValue {
   349	                            value: None,
   350	                            lamp,
   351	                            peer,
   352	                        },
   353	                    );
   354	                } else {
   355	                    let value = value.get(&*key).unwrap();
   356	                    ans.insert(
   357	                        key,
   358	                        MapValue {
   359	                            value: Some(value.clone()),
   360	                            lamp,
   361	                            peer,
   362	                        },
   363	                    );
   364	                }
   365	            }
   366	
   367	            Ok(ans)
   368	        }
   369	    }

docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). docs/architecture/ide-consumer-contract.md:42:`WorkbookRuntime` is **per-edit**, not per-session. It borrows `&mut wb` + `&reg` + `&mut oplog` for the duration of one user action (one set_formula call, one paste transaction, one recompute). Borrowing `&mut wb` for the runtime's lifetime prevents the IDE from reading the workbook through other paths while an edit is in flight — that's intentional. The IDE typically constructs a runtime, performs ONE operation, drops the runtime, then re-reads cells for grid rendering.

     2	//!
     3	//! **Tier D2 (2026-05-19) — Phase 4.12 Opus-C HIGH-3 closure:** this
     4	//! module moved from `ql-oplog::persistence` to `ql-io::oplog_persistence`.
     5	//! The move inverts the prior `ql-oplog → ql-io` dependency direction
     6	//! so Phase 5 CRDT integration sees `ql-oplog` as a dependency floor.
     7	//! External callers that previously imported
     8	//! `ql_oplog::save_workbook_with_oplog` (etc.) now import from
     9	//! `ql_io::oplog_persistence::*` (re-exported at `ql_io::*`).
    10	//!
    11	//! Phase 2A.3.c (2026-05-12) — original `.qbook/` ↔ op-log persistence.
    12	//!
    13	//! Adds `oplog.bin` as a sidecar file inside the `.qbook/` directory. The
    14	//! sidecar is written by `save_workbook_with_oplog` using the closure-based
    15	//! extension hook `ql_io::save_workbook_extending`, so it rides the same
    16	//! atomic-rename protocol as the envelope + sheet JSONLs. Crash recovery
    17	//! works transparently — `oplog.bin` lives inside the backup directory
    18	//! alongside the rest and recovers via `recover_from_crashed_save`.
    19	//!
    20	//! ## Sidecar filename
    21	//!
    22	//! `oplog.bin` — binary `Loro::ExportMode::Snapshot` blob (per
    23	//! [`OpLog::export_bytes`]). Versioning is handled inside the Loro snapshot
    24	//! format; this layer is content-agnostic.
    25	//!
    26	//! ## Documented behavior
    27	//!
    28	//! - `save_workbook_with_oplog` writes BOTH the workbook AND `oplog.bin`.
    29	//!   Any previously-present `oplog.bin` in the target is overwritten.
    30	//! - `load_workbook_with_oplog` reads BOTH. If `oplog.bin` is missing,
    31	//!   returns [`PersistenceError::Qbook(QbookError::MissingFile {..})`] —
    32	//!   no silent fallback to an empty op log per the no-fallbacks rule.
    33	//! - The plain `ql_io::save_workbook` (no oplog parameter) DROPS any
    34	//!   existing `oplog.bin` in the target. Callers that want to keep history
    35	//!   MUST use `save_workbook_with_oplog`. Loud: pinned by the test
    36	//!   `save_workbook_drops_existing_oplog_bin`.
    37	//! - The plain `ql_io::load_workbook` ignores any `oplog.bin` that's
    38	//!   present (returns the workbook only). Forward-compatible: a v2 reader
    39	//!   without op-log support can still read a workbook saved with an op log.
    40

    53	/// Combined error type for the persistence functions in this module. Wraps
    54	/// both [`QbookError`] (from the underlying workbook persistence) and
    55	/// [`OpLogError`] (from Loro snapshot encode/decode).
    56	#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    57	#[non_exhaustive]
    58	pub enum PersistenceError {
    59	    /// Workbook persistence layer error (I/O, schema, malformed cell, etc.).
    60	    #[error("workbook persistence error: {0}")]
    61	    Qbook(#[from] QbookError),
    62	
    63	    /// Op-log encode/decode error (Loro internal, serde_json, etc.).
    64	    #[error("op log error: {0}")]
    65	    OpLog(#[from] OpLogError),
    66	}
    67	
    68	/// Save a workbook AND its op log to `path` atomically. Both files land
    69	/// together via the `.qbook/` atomic-rename protocol — there's no window in
    70	/// which the workbook is updated but the op log isn't (or vice versa).
    71	///
    72	/// Overwrites any prior `oplog.bin` in the target.
    73	pub fn save_workbook_with_oplog(
    74	    wb: &Workbook,
    75	    oplog: &OpLog,
    76	    name: &str,
    77	    path: &Path,
    78	) -> Result<(), PersistenceError> {
    79	    // Export the Loro snapshot bytes FIRST. Failing here (e.g., a
    80	    // serde_json NaN/Inf rejection nested inside an Op::PutValue) surfaces
    81	    // before we touch the filesystem.
    82	    let bytes = oplog.export_bytes()?;
    83	
    84	    // Hand off to ql-io. The closure writes `oplog.bin` into the temp
    85	    // directory; the atomic rename then moves it into place with the rest
    86	    // of the workbook.
    87	    save_workbook_extending(wb, name, path, |temp_dir| {
    88	        fs::write(temp_dir.join(OPLOG_FILENAME), &bytes).map_err(QbookError::Io)
    89	    })?;
    90	    Ok(())
    91	}
    92	
    93	/// Load a workbook AND its op log from `path`. Both files must be present.
    94	///
    95	/// Errors:
    96	/// - [`PersistenceError::Qbook`] if the workbook itself fails to load
    97	///   (missing envelope, schema mismatch, malformed cell, etc.).
    98	/// - [`PersistenceError::Qbook(QbookError::MissingFile)`] specifically when
    99	///   `oplog.bin` is missing — the caller asked for the op log; surfacing
   100	///   the absence loudly is the no-fallbacks-rule answer.
   101	/// - [`PersistenceError::OpLog`] if `oplog.bin` is present but Loro can't
   102	///   decode it (corruption, version mismatch in the Loro snapshot format).
   103	pub fn load_workbook_with_oplog(path: &Path) -> Result<(Workbook, OpLog), PersistenceError> {
   104	    let wb = load_workbook(path)?;
   105	    let oplog_path = path.join(OPLOG_FILENAME);
   106	    if !oplog_path.is_file() {
   107	        return Err(PersistenceError::Qbook(QbookError::MissingFile {
   108	            file: oplog_path,
   109	        }));
   110	    }
   111	    let bytes = fs::read(&oplog_path).map_err(QbookError::Io)?;
   112	    let oplog = OpLog::import_bytes(&bytes)?;
   113	    Ok((wb, oplog))
   114	}

**A. Loro Integration**

A1. Correct: `LoroMap` is one value per key, with deterministic LWW by `(lamport, peer)`, not “both survive” for the same key. Evidence: `MapState` stores `map: BTreeMap<InternalString, MapValue>` in [map_state.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/state/map_state.rs:20), merge skips older values via `old_value > &value` in [map_state.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/state/map_state.rs:61), and ordering is `lamp` then `peer` in [map_delta.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/delta/map_delta.rs:26). Verdict: same key -> one value survives; distinct keys -> both survive.

A2. No heavyweight container allocation per `insert`. `doc.get_map("presence")` accesses a root container, and Loro says root container access “does not record history” in [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-1.12.0/src/lib.rs:481). `insert` emits a `MapSet { value: Some(value.clone()) }` in [handler.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/handler.rs:3981). Only `insert_container_with_txn` creates `ContainerID::new_normal` in [handler.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/handler.rs:4017). Hot-path cost is still one Loro map op + JSON serialize + commit per changed presence update.

A3. Yes: `doc.commit()` commits the cumulative pending transaction for the whole doc, not just presence. Loro says “Commit the cumulative auto commit transaction” and every operation has a transaction in [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-1.12.0/src/lib.rs:575). Current `OpLog::append` commits immediately in [log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:84), so no current in-flight ops are left to be swept up, but future batching would be coupled unless documented.

A4. This is a real design-vs-implementation contradiction. The architecture doc says “Presence updates do NOT persist across `.qbook` save/load” in [crdt-data-model.md](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/crdt-data-model.md:240). The implementation says presence “DO survive `OpLog::export_bytes` / `import_bytes`” in [presence.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/presence.rs:16), and `.qbook` persistence writes `oplog.export_bytes()` into `oplog.bin` in [oplog_persistence.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io/src/oplog_persistence.rs:82). Treat as a V1 known limitation or add filtering; do not leave both docs true.

**B. API Ergonomics**

B1. OK. `PresenceState` is `Copy` with primitive fields in [presence.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/presence.rs:61). JSON serialization dominates cost; by-value is fine.

B2. `Result<Option<PresenceState>, CollabSessionError>` is the cleaner Rust API. Missing presence is not an error, malformed present JSON is. `Option<Result<...>>` would make callers handle the fallible case less ergonomically.

B3. The 16-hex u64 key is defensible because `PeerId` is explicitly Loro-native `u64` in [peer.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/peer.rs:3). But the design doc still says UUIDs in [crdt-data-model.md](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/crdt-data-model.md:219). That is doc drift.

B4. OK. Both `presence_peers` and `peers_with_presence` document Loro iteration order and tell callers to sort in [log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:235) and [session.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/session.rs:220).
